newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Timan-Pechora oil group meets on Russian deal.
newsitem.headline: Timan-Pechora oil group meets on Russian deal.

text.p: The international Timan-Pechora oil consortium, eyeing a $40 billion deal in Russia's Far North, held talks with Russian partners on Monday to try to push the production-sharing project forward.
A source at Amoco Corp, one of the group's participants, said it was unclear how long negotiations would last or if a deal could be initialled.

The Timan-Pechora Company (TPC) also includes Exxon Corp and Texaco, Norsk Hydro ASA of Norway and Russia's Rosneft and Arkhangelskgeodobycha in a project to tap 360 million tonnes of hard-to-recover crude in Russia's Timan-Pechora basin.
A Russian source close to the talks said TPC would seek to clarify export issues and existing oil legislation, as well as the position of regional officials on the project.
Officials in the Nenets Autonomous District, also in the Far North, recommended last month that the project be terminated and handed over to Russian companies.
Rosneft, the government's agent in all production-sharing contracts, has said it is seeking a greater role in TPC.
TPC president Tom Hazen has said the deal will not proceed until export issues and Russian oil legislation are clear.
